subtitleNullable: A large financial crime-focussed graph dataset with labeled subgraphs
descriptionNullable:
"Elliptic2" is a large graph dataset. 

It contains a background graph consisting of 49M node clusters and 196M edge transactions. Within this background graph, there are 122K subgraphs labeled as suspicious or licit. Suspicious subgraphs are those which are indicative of money laundering, specifically the attempt to convert the profits gained from illegal actions into fiat currency or other cryptocurrencies. 

A possible task within the dataset is binary classification of suspicious subgraphs. 

We introduce this dataset with the hope that it will:

- Provide a real-world dataset on which subgraph learning research can be applied. 
- Provide a large dataset for scalability benchmarking of graph models. 
- Enable further subgraph learning research within the financial crime/anti-money laundering sphere. 


The accompanying [research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19109) describes the dataset further. If you use the dataset, please consider citing:

```
[1] Elliptic, www.elliptic.co.
```

```
[2] C. Bellei, M. Xu, R. Phillips, T. Robinson, M. Weber, T. Kaler, C. E. Leiserson, Arvind, J. Chen, "The Shape of Money Laundering: Subgraph Representation Learning on the Blockchain with the Elliptic2 Dataset".
```

This dataset builds on a previously released [dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ellipticco/elliptic-data-set) and associated [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.02591.pdf).
